mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent company registry in the corporate shareholder's jurisdiction of incorporation

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary in the principal's jurisdiction or Luxembourg notary if executed locally
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarisation plus Hague Apostille or consular legalization for foreign-origin powers of attorney

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all UBOs, directors, managers, and material counterparties against the CSSF PEP database, Luxembourg national financial sanctions lists, UN Security Council consolidated sanctions, EU consolidated financial sanctions, and OFAC SDN/Non-SDN lists. Any PEP flag, adverse media match, or sanctions hit triggers enhanced due diligence, source-of-wealth analysis, and escalation to the CSSF under the AML/CFT obligations of the Law of 12 November 2004.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Company names may be expressed in Luxembourgish, French, German, or any language using Latin script; non-Latin scripts must be accompanied by an official transliteration or romanization. The legal form suffix 'SARL' or 'Societe a Responsabilite Limitee' is mandatory. The name must not be misleading, must not conflict with existing names or trademarks, and must not imply an activity requiring separate authorization.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: A name reservation is valid for 90 days and cannot be extended; if incorporation is not completed within that period, a fresh name search and new negative certificate must be obtained. Upon rejection, the applicant may, within 15 days, submit a written re-examination request to the Luxembourg Business Registers, providing the official search result and any trademark/prior-use evidence. If LBR maintains the rejection, an administrative appeal may be filed with the Administrative Tribunal within three months of notification, with the Luxembourg Ministry of Justice named as the opposing party.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Limited acceptance. For an active wholesale SSD and CPU trading SARL, a pure virtual mailbox or registered-address-only office is not acceptable. A physical occupied office, serviced office, or managed premises in Luxembourg with local management, bookkeeping, bank account, and operational substance is required; otherwise the Luxembourg tax administration and the Luxembourg Business Registers may challenge the registered office and business substance.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Moderate: approximately 30-40% estimated probability of an unannounced tax, VAT, or customs-related physical inspection within the first two years of operation for an active semiconductor wholesale trader; AML/CFT on-site inspections by the CSSF are less frequent but remain possible for counterparties subject to CSSF supervision.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Luxembourg Law of 10 August 1915 on Commercial Companies, as amended (Loi modifiée du 10 août 1915 concernant les sociétés commerciales), Articles 710-1 to 710-23 governing the Société à Responsabilité Limitée (SARL); Law of 19 December 2002 on the Trade and Companies Register (Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés) and the annual accounts of undertakings; Grand-Ducal Regulation of 23 January 2003 on the electronic collection of company acts (RESA).
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) – Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS), 27-29 Boulevard Prince Henri, L-1724 Luxembourg; e-filing portal maintained by LBR.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Acte constitutif et statuts (notarized deed of incorporation and articles of association) filed with the RCS and published in the Recueil électronique des sociétés et associations (RESA).
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: Following the Law of 10 August 2016, the SARL has no statutory minimum share capital (statutory floor of EUR 1.00); the capital fixed in the articles must be fully subscribed and paid up in cash or in kind. Cash contributions must be credited to a blocked bank account opened in the company's name, with a bank attestation confirming irrevocable availability of funds; the funds are released only after RCS registration. No mandatory government escrow beyond this blocked-account mechanism.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED: (1) the entire issued share capital of EUR 100.00, divided into 100 shares of EUR 1.00 each, is subscribed in full by the incorporators; (2) the registered office is adopted at the address filed with the Luxembourg Business Registers, and the gérant is authorized to lease the premises and complete all RCS formalities; (3) [Manager Name] is appointed first gérant with sole signature power, and [Officer Name] is appointed AML and data-protection compliance officer; (4) the gérant is authorized to open bank accounts, obtain the VAT number from the AEDV, and execute all documents enabling the wholesale brokerage of solid-state drives and server processors.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Notarization of the Deed of Incorporation and Articles of Association
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg notary (Notaires du Grand-Duché de Luxembourg) acting within the RCS filing circuit
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Instruct a Luxembourg notary to draft the statuts in French or German. Foreign incorporators must deliver legalized (Apostille) powers of attorney and, if corporate shareholders, extract of the authorising board resolution. Conduct the notarial signing session, during which the notary verifies identity, the bank attestation, the corporate name availability, and the capacity of the gérant. After signature, the notary submits the electronic dossier to the RCS negative control system.
required_dossiers: Draft articles of association (statuts)
Valid passport copies of all incorporators and the gérant
Bank attestation evidencing deposit of share capital on a blocked account
Criminal record extract (bulletin n°3) of the proposed gérant
Apostilled or legalised power of attorney for each non-resident signatory
Written consent of the registered-office owner
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the RCS negative control flags the deed, the notary corrects the clauses and the incorporators re-execute the deed by addendum. A refused corporate name is replaced by a secondary name; judicial appeal lies before the Tribunal d'arrondissement (commercial chamber).

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Company Bank Account Opening and Blocked Capital Deposit
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg credit institution selected by the incorporators (bank licensed by the CSSF)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit a company account application to the chosen bank and undergo full KYC/AML due diligence on the ultimate beneficial owners, source of funds, and expected transaction flows. Deposit the minimum agreed share capital (EUR 1.00 or higher amount stated in the statuts) on a blocked escrow account to be released upon production of the RCS registration certificate. Obtain the attestation de consignation addressed to the notary.
required_dossiers: Company account application form
Executed or draft statuts
Passports and residence proofs of shareholders and managers
Source-of-wealth documentation and bank references
Short business plan describing wholesale SSD/CPU trading and counterparties
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank declines the file on AML grounds, approach a second credit institution or the Luxembourg House of Financial Technology for guidance; once an attestation is obtained, deliver a substitute certificate to the notary before the notarial signature.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: RCS Registration and Acquisition of Legal Personality
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) – Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The notary files the executed deed of incorporation, the bank attestation, the consent of officers, and RCS standard Form A through the LBR e-filing portal. Pay the registration fee. The RCS conducts negative control and, upon clearance, records the company and issues the RCS extract. Legal personality is acquired on the date of registration.
required_dossiers: Notarised deed of incorporation
RCS standard form A (appointment of gérant) duly signed
Bank attestation of capital deposit
Written consent of the gérant and each officer
Registered-office lease or owners' consent
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Respond to the RCS query letter within one month with corrected or supplementary documents; benefit from the three-month regularization window before closure; seek judicial recourse before the commercial chamber if the registry refuses registration without legal basis.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers – Recueil électronique des sociétés et associations (RESA)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After RCS registration, LBR effectuates the publication of the deed of incorporation, the shareholders, the share capital, the registered-office address, and the identities of the gérants in the RESA. Verify the published excerpt online and request rectification of any discrepancy. Publication renders the deed opposable to third parties.
required_dossiers: RCS registration extract
Notarised deed text in publication format
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: File a rectified notice through the notary for material errors; if the corporate object is misstated, amend the statuts by additional notarial deed and re-publish the corrected version.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Post-Incorporation Registrations (RBE, VAT, Social Security, Labour)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: LBR (RBE beneficial-ownership register); Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA (AEDV); Centre Commun de la Sécurité Sociale (CCSS); Inspection du Travail et des Mines (ITM)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Within one month, file the ultimate beneficial owner declarations in the RBE electronic register. Apply to the AEDV for the VAT number, describing the ISIC 4651 wholesale trading activity. Register the company with the CCSS for social security and with the ITM for workplace identification; obtain the employer registration number and, if applicable, the establishment permit for any physical premises.
required_dossiers: RCS registration extract
RBE beneficial-ownership form with identity proofs
AEDV VAT registration form (Formulaire 1) and activity description
Employment contracts and identity documents of staff
Premises occupancy certificate and electrical/safety compliance certificates
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Late RBE filing exposes the company and managers to criminal fines; file immediately with spontaneous disclosure. VAT late registration carries monthly penalties and may be regularised under the AEDV amicable settlement procedure. CCSS arrears can be consolidated into a compliance instalment plan.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Ministry of the Economy – Directorate-General for Industry and SMEs (autorisation d'établissement regime under the Law of 2 September 2011 on the access to the professions of artisan, merchant, industrialist and certain liberal professions); not applicable to pure brokerage but applicable if warehousing or physical distribution premises are added.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Not applicable – no industrial or establishment permit required for open-market brokerage of SSD and CPU chips; RCS registration and VAT number constitute the sufficient operating authorization. If warehousing is added: Establishment Permit (Autorisation d'Établissement) under the Law of 2 September 2011.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Administration de l'Environnement (Luxembourg Environmental Protection Agency), 1, avenue du Rock'n'Roll, L-4361 Esch-sur-Alzette
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Category D – Exempt from full EIA; wholesale trading and electronic component brokerage are not listed in the impact-assessment annexes of the Grand-Ducal Regulation of 10 May 1999. Registration is required only for waste electrical and electronic equipment (WEEE) obligations under the Law of 24 May 2013.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Zero process wastewater and negligible VOC emissions from pure trading operations. Office sewage discharges to the municipal network must comply with the Grand-Ducal Regulation of 15 July 1997 on wastewater treatment. If the company imports or distributes EEE, it must register under the WEEE regime, comply with RoHS Directive 2011/65/EU restricted substances limits, and arrange for recovery of any generated electronic waste; no hazardous waste storage permitted without a dedicated permit.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certification for any office or logistics premises must be issued following inspection by the communal fire prevention service (Service Incendie et de Secours), including emergency evacuation plans and alarm testing. Warehousing of high-density storage racks requires a structural load inspection certificate from an approved engineer (shelving systems rated for their design load). Occupational clearance is obtained from the Inspection du Travail et des Mines (ITM), covering workplace ergonomics, electrical installation verification, and thermal management for rooms holding servers or electronic equipment; a standing workplace register and annual safety audit are required.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Administration des contributions directes (ACD) for corporate income tax matters and Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA (AED) for VAT matters. Electronic access is consolidated via the national business and tax portal myGuichet.lu (guichet.public.lu), complemented by the Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) company file and the AED VAT e-filing systems.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign entity establishing a Luxembourg SARL must first complete commercial registration with the Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) and obtain a national identification number (matricule). For direct VAT registration without a permanent establishment, a non-resident taxable person must file Form 642 with the AED and submit the constitutive documents, powers of attorney, and evidence of the foreign VAT ID, where applicable. Corporate income tax registration is effected through the annual corporate tax return filing procedure with the ACD, using the matricule as the tax identification number. A Luxembourg VAT identification number is then issued by the AED for all taxable supplies effected in Luxembourg.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No check-the-box transparency election exists under Luxembourg domestic law; SARLs are opaque corporations taxed at entity level. The Luxembourg fiscal unity regime allows a 95%-owned subsidiary to consolidate corporate income tax with its resident parent where both entities are resident companies. A separate VAT group election is available for closely connected persons established in Luxembourg. Anti-hybrid rules under EU ATAD apply, with no elective hybrid mismatch characterisation permitted.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: No registration threshold for non-established taxable persons supplying goods in Luxembourg; any taxable supply triggers VAT registration. Domestic small enterprises with annual turnover not exceeding EUR 35,000 may benefit from the Luxembourg small business exemption, but that exemption is inapplicable to cross-border wholesale semiconductor trading.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No real-time fiscal clearance or digital stamping regime applies in Luxembourg as of 2025. E-invoicing is permitted and treated as equivalent to paper invoices where authenticity of origin, integrity, and readability are preserved. Mandatory B2G electronic invoicing applies to central government contracts through PEPPOL BIS 3.0. VAT returns and recapitulative statements must be filed electronically through myGuichet.lu or the AED portal; SAP-based clearance and API stamping are not yet required for wholesale supplies.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero rating applies to the supply of goods physically exported from Luxembourg or from another EU member state by the vendor or on its behalf to a destination outside the EU. For a wholesale SSD and server processor trader, the vendor must hold evidence of dispatch or transport out of the EU, the customer must be established outside the EU or otherwise export the goods, and title in the goods must pass to the non-EU customer. No VAT is charged where the export documentation is complete, and the related input VAT is separately recoverable by the taxable person.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (the automated export system SAD/EX declaration with MRN)
Bill of Lading or Airway Bill evidencing physical departure from the EU
Inward Remittance Certificate or bank transfer receipt evidencing FX repatriation to Luxembourg
Commercial invoice and purchase order references
Incoterms-based proof of delivery and dispatch documents
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The Luxembourg tax authorities and customs administration cross-match VAT export records with ECB and bank payment data, transport documents, and consignee registries. Where export zero-rating is inadequately substantiated or where goods fail to leave the EU within the statutory export period, the AED disallows the zero rate and assesses the VAT that should have been declared. Fraudulent claims expose the taxable person to retroactive VAT collection, late interest at 0.8% per month, administrative fines, and, in severe cases, criminal penalties under Luxembourg tax and customs law. For wholesale semiconductor transactions, export compliance documentation must be retained for at least ten years.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque centrale du Luxembourg (BCL), operating within the Eurosystem framework of the European Central Bank (ECB); banking prudential supervision is exercised by the Commission de Surveillance du Secteur Financier (CSSF).
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Luxembourg is a Eurozone member with full current-account and capital-account convertibility. The euro is freely convertible; there are no exchange controls, no restrictions on profit remittance, dividend distributions, or repatriation of capital for non-resident shareholders. EU free-movement-of-capital rules apply. Only statistical Balance of Payments declarations are required for cross-border transfers exceeding EUR 12,500, a reporting function discharged by the resident banking institution.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: None. Luxembourg imposes no statutory timeline for export-receipt repatriation and no mandatory conversion ratio. Export proceeds may be retained in EUR or held in USD, CNY, TWD, KRW, or other freely convertible currencies at the SARL's disposal, subject only to standard AML/CFT bookkeeping and tax documentation requirements.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Blocked Account (compte séquestre) / Operational Transaction Account

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Banque et Caisse d'Épargne de l'État (BCEE / Spuerkeess)
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Blocked Account / Operational Transaction Account
Operational Transaction Account / Escrow Séquestre Account

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Medium feasibility, subject to strict legal constraints. The SARL may use only a Luxembourg-licensed Electronic Money Institution (EMI) or Payment Institution authorized by the CSSF under PSD2, or an EU-passported EMI/PI under the passporting regime. Offshore non-EU digital EMIs, including UK post-Brexit firms without a Luxembourg branch or EU passport, are not permissible as the primary treasury rail; they cannot provide capital-blocked or escrow accounts (compte séquestre), which require a regulated credit institution. An EU-licensed EMI may support ancillary collections, FX conversion, and cross-border payment initiation, but high-value SSD/CPU trade settlements and escrow releases must be executed through a Tier-1 credit institution to preserve counterparty safety and AML integrity.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Luxembourg banking practice requires physical identity verification of account signatories. At least one authorized director/manager (gérant) of the SARL must normally appear in person at a Luxembourg branch, or attend before an EEA notary, consular officer, or certified correspondent bank where physical distance prevents direct appearance. CSSF has progressively accepted supervised video identification for EU/EEA natural persons for remote onboarding, but the baseline remains an in-person KYC interview and wet-ink or e-signature mandate. A workable alternative is the appointment of a Luxembourg-based authorized representative or power-of-attorney holder to complete the interview and sign the mandate on behalf of the board.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Semiconductor wholesale (SSD/CPU) is classified as a Medium-Risk Enhanced-Scrutiny profile under Luxembourg AML/CFT laws (CSSF Regulation 12-02 and Loi du 12 novembre 2004), particularly where high-frequency, high-value trade flows may obscure the beneficial-owner chain.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Complete trade-chain file: signed purchase orders, proforma and commercial invoices, packing lists, transport documents (bill of lading or airway bill), customs declarations (EU SAD/EXA), independent inspection certificates (SGS/BSI), end-user attestations, and a narrative business plan demonstrating physical goods flow; plus sanctions-screening outputs for every counterparty and RCS extracts of all counterparties.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Inbound capital injection from offshore, low-tax, or high-risk jurisdictions into a Luxembourg SARL holding minimal share capital (EUR 12,000) and projecting disproportionate turnover.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified constitutional documents of the shareholder, identity of all UBOs with apostille or consular legalization, source-of-wealth and source-of-funds statements, shareholder resolution authorizing the capital injection, notarial deed of incorporation, certificate of deposit issued by the receiving bank, and proof of Luxembourg economic substance (office lease, local management, payroll, bank mandate).

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Reported commercial model as open-market broker in goods that do not physically transit Luxembourg, creating mismatch between the declared intermediary role and Swift_TT / Escrow_Inspection_Wire payment rails.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Signed brokerage/intermediation/escrow agreements, principal mandates from buyers and suppliers, invoices issued by the SARL (with VAT treatment under EU Article 141 or export zero-rating), insurance certificates showing risk transfer, warehouse or inspection receipts, and a clear representation of the contract chain in the BCL Balance of Payments statistical coding (goods turnover versus commissions).

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound shareholder capital is routed via SWIFT MT103 customer credit transfer to the SARL's blocked capital account (compte séquestre) opened at the Luxembourg bank before notarial execution. Field 70 (Remittance Information) must state: 'CAPITAL CONTRIBUTION — SUBSCRIPTION OF SHARES — [NOTARIAL DEED DATE] / [SHAREHOLDER RESOLUTION REF]'. The beneficiary bank applies the BCL Balance of Payments purpose code for direct investment (equity capital) for EU statistical reporting. Verification package: authenticated shareholders' resolution, notarial deed of incorporation, subscribed share ledger, certificate of deposit, and RCS registration extract. No central-bank approval is required; available funds are released to the operational account immediately upon registration in the Luxembourg Trade and Companies Register (RCS).
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Primary clearing rail: SWIFT MT103 customer credit transfers in USD or EUR for supplier payments, with invoice numbers, INCO terms, and goods description (ISIC 4651 semiconductors) cited in field 70, and BCL purpose code 'Payment for goods'. Secondary rail: irrevocable Commercial Letters of Credit (UCP600), issued, advised, or confirmed by a Luxembourg bank, requiring commercial invoice, clean on-board bill of lading or airway bill, packing list, certificate of origin, and inspection certificate for large-ticket trades. Escrow-inspection wires: settlement from the buyer to the supplier is released through a segregated séquestre account at the Luxembourg bank upon presentation of an agreed independent inspection certificate (SGS or equivalent) and fulfilment of the escrow mandate; all release conditions are documented in a tripartite escrow agreement.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable FX spot and outright FX forward contracts (EUR/USD, EUR/CNY-CNH, EUR/TWD, EUR/KRW where offered) for hedging transactional trade exposure

Non-deliverable forward (NDF) contracts referencing CNY, TWD, and KRW, permitted only for hedging genuine commercial trade exposures and executed under a master FX agreement with an EU-regulated counterparty
FX swaps (short-dated rollover) to optimize intra-month liquidity and settle offsetting USD/EUR receivables and payables

Cross-currency interest rate swaps (CCIRS) for long-term shareholder or intra-group funding liabilities; all derivative instruments require an approved ISDA/CSA or local master agreement, board treasury policy adoption, and EMIR reporting compliance

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual RCS confirmation (confirmation annuelle) of register data
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) – Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within one calendar month following the annual anniversary of the company’s RCS registration; anniversary-based, no fixed calendar date
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Written reminder by LBR; if still outstanding, Commercial Court may intervene; directors face administrative fines of EUR 500–EUR 5,000; persistent default may be sanctioned by judicial strike-off/dissolution.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual accounts (financial statements) filing and publication
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) – RCS, via eJust electronic filing
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within seven months after the end of the financial year; for a 31 December year-end, no later than 31 July of the following calendar year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late or non-publication results in a public notice of default on the LBR/RCS portal, fines up to EUR 5,000 imposed on directors/officers, and court-ordered filing; repeated failure may ground judicial liquidation.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual confirmation/update of Ultimate Beneficial Owner (UBO) register file
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers – Registre des bénéficiaires effectifs (RBE / UBO Registrar)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: At least once per year, within one month following the anniversary of the most recent UBO declaration/confirmation; any UBO change from share transfers must be filed within one month of the triggering event
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Criminal penalties under the amended Law of 13 January 2019 including fines up to EUR 125,000 for legal persons and imprisonment/fines for responsible officers; LBR may also flag the company’s file for non-resolution.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: A statutory audit by an approved réviseur d’entreprises is mandatory when the SARL exceeds two of the following three thresholds for two consecutive financial years: balance-sheet total EUR 4.4 million, net turnover EUR 8.8 million, average annual employees 50; also mandatory for public-interest entities and in other specific cases.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Luxembourg GAAP under the Law of 19 December 2002, as amended; IFRS as adopted by the EU is permitted/relevant for certain entities and required for listed safer companies.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Each SARL must maintain a UBO register at the registered office and ensure that the information filed with the RBE is accurate. Confirmation is mandatory at least once per calendar year and is due within one month after the anniversary of the initial/previous UBO declaration. Shareholding transfers must be recorded in the annual confirmation or, if they change beneficial ownership, in a separate update filed with the RBE within one month of the transfer.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Members (shareholders and share transfers)
Minute Book (general meetings and management decisions)

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 1,900–5,400 per year for commercial domiciliation/registered-office agent services (EUR 1,600–4,500)
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 8,400–27,000 for a statutory audit of a wholesale trading SARL under Luxembourg GAAP (EUR 7,500–24,000)

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 17% standard corporate income tax (IRC) for taxable income above EUR 200,000; plus 7% unemployment solidarity surcharge and municipal business tax (standard Luxembourg City rate 6.75%), producing an aggregate effective Luxembourg City rate of approximately 24.94%.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: 80% exemption for qualifying net intellectual property income and capital gains under the Luxembourg IP box regime; 100% participation exemption on qualifying dividends and capital gains (minimum 10% shareholding or EUR 1.2 million acquisition cost, 12-month holding period); technology and innovation investment credit; no statutory Luxembourg withholding tax on arm's-length outbound royalties or interest; full exemption available for qualifying EU parent-subsidiary dividends.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Formulaire 700 — Corporate Income Tax Return (integrated with Luxembourg municipal business tax and net wealth tax), filed electronically through MyGuichet.lu or the Luxembourg Direct Tax Administration's certified e-filing portal.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Due by 31 May following the fiscal year-end unless a valid extension is granted by the Luxembourg Direct Tax Administration; quarterly prepayments of corporate income tax and municipal business tax are due on 9 February, 9 May, 9 August and 9 November.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Legal name of the SARL, Luxembourg Business Register (RCS) number, tax identification number, registered office address, legal form and principal business activity code (ISIC 4651 / NAICS 423430).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: If a non-resident company carries on wholesale SSD/CPU trading through a Luxembourg permanent establishment, enter PE registration details and maintain separate accounts; a non-resident shareholder not commercially active through Luxembourg does not file this return in the SARL's place.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net profit or loss before tax reconciled with statutory annual accounts, including inventory valuation, trade receivables, and spot-market positions in semiconductor goods.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Attach local statutory branch accounts and remove head-office general and administrative income not functionally attributable to the Luxembourg PE.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box B.20 / Tax-exempt income and participation exemption
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Separate declaration of exempt dividends, exempt capital gains, IP box income, and similar relief items that reduce the corporate income tax base.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident PE must evidence that exemption items are economically connected to Luxembourg PE activities and supported by qualifying shareholding or qualifying IP records.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box B.30 / Non-deductible expenses and add-backs
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Enter disallowed expenses, excessive management fees, interest that fails thin-capitalization tests, certain representation expenses, and transfer pricing adjustments.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For non-resident controlled transactions, attach contemporaneous transfer pricing documentation to justify the arm's-length nature of SSD/CPU procurement, sale and brokerage commission flows.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box B.40 / Tax losses carried forward
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: State the amount of prior-year tax losses utilized in the current year, supported by a reconciliation of the loss carryforward schedule.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Loss carryforward of a Luxembourg PE may be used only if the PE was continuously taxable in Luxembourg and the loss relates exclusively to PE-proper activities.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box C / Tax computation and withholding credits
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Computation of taxable result, corporate income tax at 17%, solidarity surcharge, municipal business tax, estimated prepayments and any foreign tax credits.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident PE must attach a statement of Luxembourg-source income only and evidence any source-country withholding tax credit under a double tax treaty.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Declaration of dividends resolved or paid during the accounting year, applicable dividend withholding tax, and details of each shareholder.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For a non-resident shareholder claiming treaty relief, attach the shareholder's valid tax residence certificate and beneficial ownership declaration to the extended Form 700 filing prerequisites or the withholding tax refund claim.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late Form 700 filing triggers an administrative penalty generally up to EUR 5,000, late-payment interest at statutory monthly rates, and possible default assessment by the Luxembourg tax authorities; intentional concealment under Luxembourg General Tax Law may expose the entity to a criminal fine of up to EUR 250,000 and imprisonment of up to five years.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 15% domestic dividend withholding tax on distributions by a Luxembourg SARL; reduced to 0% for qualifying EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive shareholders (at least 10% holding for 12 months); double tax treaties generally reduce the rate to 0%, 5% or 15% depending on shareholding percentage and treaty partner.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To obtain treaty relief, the non-resident beneficial owner must submit to the Luxembourg paying agent a current tax residence certificate (TRC), a signed written declaration of beneficial entitlement, and confirmation of shareholding period before the dividend payment date. Relief at source is processed through the standard Luxembourg withholding tax reduction application; where tax has been over-withheld, a refund claim must be filed with the Luxembourg Direct Tax Administration within the statutory claim period using the prescribed forms and supporting TRC.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Luxembourg domestic law imposes no withholding tax on outbound arm's-length interest or royalties, therefore the statutory rate is 0% for both ordinary corporate debt interest and IP royalties; treaty rates are generally redundant and also 0%, subject to anti-conduit and beneficial ownership requirements under the OECD Multilateral Instrument and Luxembourg GAAR.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Mandatory local file and master file documentation required for controlled transactions where annual related-party transaction value exceeds EUR 1,000,000; Country-by-Country Reporting applies where the consolidated group revenue reaches EUR 750,000,000 or more.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Luxembourg does not enforce offshore Economic Substance Regulations as a separate statute, but the Luxembourg tax residence, effective management, GAAR, anti-abuse, BEPS and ATAD rules require real economic substance. For the SARL's wholesale SSD/CPU brokerage business, the company must maintain employees executing contracts, tax-resident board decision-making, physical storage or logistics arrangements, independent treasury control, contemporaneous transfer pricing documents, and accounting evidence in Luxembourg; otherwise the Luxembourg tax administration may disregard the entity, deny treaty application, reattribute profits, or assess a permanent establishment of the non-resident owner.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Tax evasion / fraudulent corporate income tax return
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Recording fictitious purchases or inflated cost of goods sold from shell suppliers, under-declaring spot SSD/CPU resale proceeds, using unsubstantiated cash sales, or shifting profits to related parties without valid commercial purpose.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Reassessment of taxable income, 10% tax fraud penalty or criminal fine up to EUR 250,000, accrual of late interest, and imprisonment of up to five years for natural persons under the Luxembourg General Tax Law.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who sign fraudulent statements or approve false invoices are jointly and severally liable for the tax shortfall, may be subject to civil restitution, travel bans, frozen bank accounts, disqualification from management, and imprisonment upon criminal conviction.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell company / lack of economic substance
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using the Luxembourg SARL solely as a letterbox entity with no employees, no operational management, no real wholesale trading functions, no physical storage or risk-taking, and routing semiconductor profits through low-tax jurisdictions without substance.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The Luxembourg tax administration may disregard the entity, re-assign profits to the effective-manager jurisdiction, deny participation exemption and treaty benefits, impose transfer pricing adjustments, and, under commercial law, apply corporate dissolution or strike-off procedures for companies that become mere shells.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Nominee directors and beneficial owners may be held personally liable when the shell was used to commit tax fraud or mislead third-party creditors and tax authorities; civil liability, director disqualification, travel bans, asset seizures and money-laundering criminal liability are available.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: AML-CFT non-compliance and trade-based money laundering
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Accepting cash settlements for high-value chip trading, structuring wire transfers below reporting thresholds, conducting transactions with shell banks or crypto intermediaries, concealing ultimate beneficial ownership, or trading with entities connected to sanctioned jurisdictions without a Luxembourg AML risk assessment.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Luxembourg AML law empowers the Financial Intelligence Unit and professionals supervisory authority to impose regulatory fines up to EUR 5,000,000 or 5% of annual turnover; criminal money-laundering sanctions include forced confiscation of assets, fines, freezing orders and imprisonment up to five years; underlying tax consequences include full reassessment and penalty stacking.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who knowingly perform or facilitate trade-based money laundering can be criminally prosecuted individually, subjected to asset freezing and travel bans, ordered to pay civil compensation, held personally liable for fines not covered by the entity, and permanently disqualified from managing Luxembourg companies.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Transfer pricing documentation failure / artificial profit shifting
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failure to maintain contemporaneous arm's-length documentation for intercompany chip purchases, commission payments, intellectual property royalties, or intra-group financing; executing undocumented back-to-back transactions with no function-and-risk analysis; pricing inventory without a recognized transfer pricing method.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: A transfer pricing audit adjustment increases the Luxembourg taxable base; a documentation penalty may be imposed separately, late interest accumulates, and tax treaty benefits may be denied under the Limitation on Benefits clauses or the Principal Purpose Test; monetary penalties can reach EUR 250,000 in aggravated cases.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors responsible for the transfer pricing policy may be personally liable for fraudulent misrepresentations made to the tax administration, may be summoned for tax criminal proceedings, and can face personal seizure of assets or travel restrictions where the profit shift was knowingly supported by false documents.
